chunks: When 'Alī عليه السلام had finished with the people of al-Baṣrah, seventy men from the Zutt came to him, greeted him, and spoke to him in their language.
Then he said to them: Indeed, I am not as you have said; I am a servant of Allah, created.
He said: But they refused him and said—may Allah curse them—No, rather you are, you are He.
So he said to them: If you do not return from what you have said and do not repent to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, I will surely kill you.
He said: But they refused to repent and return.

He said: Then he عليه السلام ordered that wells be dug for them, so they were dug. Then he opened some of them into others, then cast them into them, then covered their tops. Then he kindled a fire in one well among them while none of them was in it, so the smoke entered upon them and they died.

key_terms.الدُّخَانُ: smoke; the means by which they died in the pits
key_terms.الزُّطِّ: the Zutt; the group from whom the seventy men came
key_terms.تَتُوبُوا: repent; to turn back to Allah from false belief
key_terms.تَرْجِعُوا: return; to withdraw from the statement they had made
key_terms.عَبْدُ اللَّهِ: a servant of Allah; Imam 'Alī عليه السلام identifies himself as a created servant, rejecting divinity

ai.seo_question: What did Imam 'Alī عليه السلام do when some people claimed that he was divine?
ai.summary: This report recounts an incident in which a group attributed divinity to Imam 'Alī عليه السلام, and he explicitly rejected their claim by affirming that he was a created servant of Allah. When they persisted and refused tawbah, he punished them, making the narration significant for questions of tawhid, ghuluw, and apostasy.
